data.part_b: What is the range of the household's monthly electricity use?
data.part_c: What is the period of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the household's electricity use in August. Round to the nearest kilowatt-hour.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline y=D is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=769, so the household averages \boxed{769\text{ kWh}} per month.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=@A@, so the quantity rises @A@ above the average value and falls @A@ below it:

\text{maximum}=769+94=863\text{ kWh}\qquad \text{minimum}=769-94=675\text{ kWh}

the heaviest use is in June at 863\text{ kWh} and the lightest is in December at 675\text{ kWh}, so the range of monthly use is \boxed{[675\text{ kWh},\ 863\text{ kWh}]}.

Part (c). Here B= rac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\frac{\pi}{6}}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} @index_unit@, and so use follows a yearly cycle and repeats every 12 months.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of @var@ that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-3)=0 \implies x-3=0 \implies x=3

The phase shift is \boxed{3} months, and so the pattern is shifted 3 months to the right: use is at its average and rising in March, peaks in June, and bottoms out in December.

Part (e). Substitute x=8 (August):

E(8)=94\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(8-3)\right]+769=94\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+769=863\text{ kWh}

So the model predicts about \boxed{863\text{ kWh}} of use in August.
